purpose: Represents a full TSN usecase instance combining topology, streams, and configuration (i.e. scheduling). It acts as the central orchestration object connecting setup (UsecaseConfig), network topology (NetworkX graph via TopologyHandler), traffic streams (Stream), and scheduling (Schedule).

data_model.Usecase: Core container object holding a network graph, stream set, and configuration state. Encodes full simulation or optimization instance.
data_model.graph: NetworkX directed graph with TSN port-aware metadata (ingress/egress ports per node).
data_model.streams: List of Stream objects representing traffic flows embedded into the topology.
data_model.specification: UsecaseConfig defining topology and traffic generation parameters.
data_model.configuration: Schedule, offset, and latency information for each stream.

responsibilities: Initialize TSN instance from config file
Generate or load network topology
Generate traffic streams and embed them into topology
Expose derived network properties (ports, hosts, switches, links)
Compute macro-cycle based on stream periods
Interface with scheduling system (Schedule)
Apply and remove schedules from graph and streams
Serialize and deserialize full usecase state
Provide utility mappings between port names and IDs

purpose: Core orchestration class that binds together TSN topology, traffic streams, and scheduling. It manages full lifecycle of a TSN scenario including generation, modification, scheduling, serialization, and analysis.
responsibilities: Load or generate UsecaseConfig from file
Construct TSN topology graph via TopologyHandler
Generate and embed Stream objects into topology
Maintain global stream list and graph consistency
Provide derived views of topology (ports, hosts, switches, links)
Compute macro-cycle from stream intervals
Expose port mapping utilities for scheduling
Generate and remove schedules from graph and streams
Update graph with scheduling information
Propagate schedule results back into streams
Compute utilization metrics per port and globally
Support stream addition and removal
Support link addition and removal in topology
Serialize full usecase state to JSON
Deserialize usecase from JSON while restoring graph-stream binding

index.purpose: Unique identifier for each Usecase instance

specsFile.purpose: Path to specification file used for usecase initialization

specification.purpose: Specification object defining topology and traffic generation parameters

graph.purpose: Network topology graph with TSN port-aware metadata

streams.purpose: List of traffic streams embedded into the topology

n_streams.purpose: Number of streams in the usecase

n_ports.purpose: Number of ports in the topology

hosts.purpose: List of host nodes in the graph

switches.purpose: List of switch nodes in the graph

links.purpose: List of links in the topology graph with metadata

macro_cycle.purpose: Least common multiple of all stream intervals defining global repetition cycle

ports.purpose: Derived mapping of all ingress and egress ports with metadata

port_name_id_mapping.purpose: Bidirectional mapping between port names and port integer IDs

streams_by_source_port.purpose: Grouping of streams by their talker/source port

task.purpose: Derived flags controlling routing and scheduling modes. First bool indicates whether routing is needed, second bool indicates whether task (talker/listener) placement is needed

schedule.purpose: Generated schedule from current streams and topology

utilization.purpose: Global and per-port utilization of scheduled transmission windows

distance_to_hosts.purpose: Shortest distances from each host to all reachable nodes

name: __post_init__
purpose: Initializes the Usecase after dataclass construction by loading specifications, building the topology graph, and optionally generating streams if none are provided.
responsibilities: Load UsecaseConfig from file if specification is not provided
Construct NetworkX topology graph via TopologyHandler
Auto-generate streams based on specifications
Ensure Usecase is fully initialized and runnable immediately after instantiation
logic_flow: If specification is None → load from specsFile
If graph is missing → build topology using TopologyHandler.makeTopology
If streams list is empty → generate streams using add_stream()

name: add_stream
purpose: Generates a new Stream and embeds it into the topology graph while maintaining consistency with current network load.
responsibilities: Generate a new Stream using Stream.generate based on the specification
Embed the stream into the topology using TrafficHandler.embed_to_topology
Append the resulting Stream to the Usecase.streams list
Ensure stream placement respects current network load
execution_flow: Generate raw Stream from specification
Call TrafficHandler.embed_to_topology with graph and current streams
Append embedded stream to streams list
side_effects: Updates stream embedding in topology context

name: remove_streams
purpose: Removes selected streams from the Usecase by their indices in the streams list.
responsibilities: Delete streams at specified indices from the streams list
Maintain list integrity after removal
execution_flow: Sort stream_ids in descending order
Delete each stream at the given index from self.streams
side_effects: Changes stream ordering implicitly due to index shifts

name: add_link
purpose: Adds a new link between two nodes in the topology graph while respecting the current Usecase specification.
responsibilities: Insert a new edge into the NetworkX topology graph
Ensure link creation follows rules defined in TopologyHandler
Update topology structure based on specification constraints
execution_flow: Call TopologyHandler.add_link with graph, specification, src, dst
side_effects: Mutates the topology graph by adding an edge

name: remove_link
purpose: Removes a link (edge) from the topology graph and updates stream routing consistency accordingly.
responsibilities: Remove an edge from the NetworkX topology graph
Ensure stream-level consistency after topology modification
Delegate removal logic to TopologyHandler
execution_flow: Call TopologyHandler.remove_link with graph, streams, src, dst
TopologyHandler handles graph update and stream consistency updates

name: addSchedule
purpose: Applies a computed schedule to the Usecase by updating both the topology graph and stream metadata.
responsibilities: Clear any existing schedule before applying a new one
Update graph with scheduling information
Update streams with schedule results (offsets, latencies, assignments)
Maintain consistency between graph, ports, and streams
execution_flow: Call removeSchedule() to clear existing scheduling state
Retrieve port_id_to_name mapping
Apply schedule to graph via schedule.update_graph
Apply schedule to streams via schedule.update_streams
side_effects: Mutates graph by adding scheduling metadata

name: removeSchedule
purpose: Removes all scheduling-related information from the topology graph and resets stream scheduling state.
responsibilities: Clear scheduling metadata from all egress ports in the graph
Reset stream-level scheduling fields (offset, accumulated latency)
Restore Usecase to an unscheduled state
execution_flow: Iterate over all graph nodes
For each egress port, remove schedule-related fields
Iterate over all streams
Reset offset and accLatency to None
side_effects: Mutates graph by removing schedule metadata

name: to_file
purpose: Serializes the entire Usecase object into JSON format and writes it to a file.
responsibilities: Generate JSON representation of the Usecase using dataclass serialization
Determine output filename if not provided
Write serialized data to disk
execution_flow: If ucFileName is None → derive filename from specification.graph_config
Call self.to_json() to serialize object
Write JSON string to file at jsnPath
Return filename used

name: from_json
purpose: Reconstructs a Usecase instance from a serialized JSON dictionary, restoring topology, streams, and graph-stream consistency.
responsibilities: Decode the NetworkX graph from serialized format
Reconstruct Stream objects from dictionaries
Create a new Usecase instance with restored streams and index
Replace post_init-generated graph with deserialized graph
Restore stream-to-graph binding for streams missing customGraph
execution_flow: Decode graph using TopologyHandler.graph_decoder
Convert stream dictionaries into Stream objects
Instantiate Usecase with specsFile, index, and streams
Overwrite generated graph with decoded graph
Ensure each stream has correct customGraph reference
side_effects: Reconstructs full object state from external data
Mutates streams to bind them to restored graph
